headline: 844 children die as measles outbreak worsens in Bangladesh
summary: Four more children died in 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 844 this year.
details: Four children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am today, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the country's combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 844 for the year.
Of these fatalities, 748 are classified as suspected measles deaths, while 96 have been laboratory-confirmed.
The DGHS also reported 1,022 new suspected cases in the same 24-hour period, raising the cumulative nationwide total to 130,083.
Additionally, 115 new laboratory-confirmed cases were recorded, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 16,295.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 112,620 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country.
According to DGHS data, 108,283 of those hospitalised patients have recovered.
caption:
844 children have died from measles and suspected measles in Bangladesh this year.

Four children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am today, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

This brings the country's combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 844 for the year.

Of these fatalities, 748 are classified as suspected measles deaths, while 96 have been laboratory-confirmed.

The DGHS also reported 1,022 new suspected cases in the same 24-hour period, raising the cumulative nationwide total to 130,083.

Additionally, 115 new laboratory-confirmed cases were recorded, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 16,295.

Since March 15, 2026, a total of 112,620 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country.

According to DGHS data, 108,283 of those hospitalised patients have recovered.

headline_marked: ACC says [[no official word on Benazir's bail]] in Dubai
headline: ACC says no official word on Benazir's bail in Dubai
summary: Anti-Corruption Commission DG Mir Mohammad Zainul Abedin Shibli says the commission has only learned of the former IGP's reported release through media reports.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has not yet received any official information regarding the reported bail of former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed in Dubai.
ACC Director General Mir Mohammad Zainul Abedin Shibli stated that while they have no official confirmation, the commission will take all necessary legal steps in accordance with the law.
The commission learned of the reported release through media reports rather than official channels.
According to various media reports, a court in the United Arab Emirates granted Benazir bail on July 27 and he was completed legal formalities and was released from custody on July 30.
DG Shibli rejected allegations of negligence, asserting that there had been no lapse on the part of the commission in handling the matter.
caption:
Former IGP Benazir Ahmed reportedly released on bail in Dubai, but the ACC says they have no official word yet.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has not yet received any official information regarding the reported bail of former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed in Dubai.

ACC Director General Mir Mohammad Zainul Abedin Shibli stated that while they have no official confirmation, the commission will take all necessary legal steps in accordance with the law.

The commission learned of the reported release through media reports rather than official channels.

According to various media reports, a court in the United Arab Emirates granted Benazir bail on July 27 and he was completed legal formalities and was released from custody on July 30.

DG Shibli rejected allegations of negligence, asserting that there had been no lapse on the part of the commission in handling the matter.
